questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A course on minds and machines (ended up not being offered)

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great university and a great city to study in.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an orientation that covered the most important things.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The orientation did not leave anything left to be desired.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very hard. AirBnB has some options further away from campus but the subway is a great way to travel (and read/study in transit)

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is expensive and not easy to find. Better off looking for something early.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Colleges are only available to domestic students which is problematic.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You show up to orientation to be registred and there is a pretty simple formula online to register for courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Email and office hours.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You might not be able to get all the courses that you see in the course catalogue so be sure that you have back up courses you are fine with taking. It is very normal for students in Toronto to go outside there field to meet breadth requirements and as such there are a lot of courses that are beginner friendly.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It depends a lot on the course. It seems there is a lot of diversity in the ways in which the courses are ran.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had a single introductory course and the rest were either second or third year courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A lot bigger classes with less engagement from students. People meet minimal requirements for the courses and don't seem to know the material. At home it is more streamlined and more prerequisites are required.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Ethics: Death and Dying, Social and Cultural Theory, Introduction to Chinese Philosophy, Freedom, Responsibility, and Human Action.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Freedom, Responsibility, and Human Action. A very concise and great course on free will. Martin Pickavé is an excellent professor and the syllabus is very carefully selected. It will give you exactly what you need to get into the subject with out being to much of a work load.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: If you don't have a Canadian credit card the fees will add up to a lot.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Generally, groceries are more expensive than expected and street food is less expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A ton of clubs and lots of events.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Most sports, board games, martial arts, video games etc. Different locally driven bars. Different department-specific events like book sales.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Escape rooms are abundant and cheap – they are a good way to bond with people you don't know too well. Go up the CN tower at least once, go watch ice hockey, football and baseball.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the distillery district on weekends, or Maddison's. In reading week, Banff is a beautiful place to go. It is also a lovely town.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Took a couple of days to orient myself but after that very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Download WhatsApp.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The classes are all very divided, it seems more individualized.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: There is so much diversity and with it so many things to do and try and taste.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Download WhatsApp, Get your T-card early, Get a bike plan.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Kennsington Market and Spadina has some great food. Record stores have a lot bigger selection than here in Copenhagen. Explore!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Doing things with new friends and exploring on my own/learning how to study in a new place.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being willing to take some risks and do stuff you wouldn't normally do at home. Getting out your comfort zone.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Toronto is so huge so start exploring early, once you are done with your exam you'll wish you had more time to do stuff in the city.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
